recentItems.title: RUSSIA rejects PEACE: THE KREMLIN IS TERRIFIED OF A PAUSE! Patriot production in Ukraine approves!
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian long-range drones struck strategic plants and oil-refining facilities in three Russian cities at once — Perm, Ulyanovsk, and Voronezh — while Russian forces attacked civilian neighborhoods in Kyiv with drones.

At the same time, Donald Trump officially supported granting Ukraine licenses to produce Patriot systems and missiles domestically, laying the groundwork for the creation of an autonomous air-defense shield.

On the diplomatic front, Washington is promoting an initiative for a limited ceasefire that would halt strikes on energy infrastructure. Moscow, however, is rejecting any pause in hostilities for the sake of negotiations.

recentItems.title: BLACK WEEK FOR PUTIN: 377 artillery systems, 24 air defense systems & refinery paralysis in Russia!
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian drones halted oil processing at Moscow’s key refinery, which supplied 40% of the city’s fuel needs, and hit three other major Russian plants. Meanwhile, Ukraine’s State Border Guard Service destroyed an enemy radar system worth approximately $100 million with a single drone, while the Security Service of Ukraine in Rostov eliminated Antonov transport aircraft that are indispensable to Russia’s military-industrial complex.

Over the past week, the Russian army lost 10,490 personnel, 377 artillery systems, and 24 air-defense systems, surpassing historic milestones of 50,000 artillery pieces and 150,000 trucks destroyed. Analyst Henry Keen assessed the Kremlin’s losses, amounting to billions of dollars, and presented a new Ukrainian-made interceptor designed to take down the enemy’s jet-powered drones.

recentItems.title: PUTIN IS LYING WHILE MILITARY INDUSTRY COLLAPSES! Ukraine launches a new phase of DEEP STRIKES
recentItems.description:
Moscow’s claims that strikes deep inside Russia change nothing are being contradicted by reality: the Deep Strikes campaign has already stretched the enemy’s scarce air-defense systems — including the S-300, S-400, and Pantsir — across thousands of kilometers, leaving the front line exposed. The destruction of equipment at major oil refineries has also caused fuel shortages and losses for the Russian budget. On top of that, the cost imbalance — shooting down cheap drones with missiles worth millions of dollars — is steadily depleting the aggressor’s stockpiles.

Ukraine is now moving to a new phase of combined missile-and-drone strikes. The use of heavy cruise missiles, including the Neptune and Flamingo, as well as domestically produced ballistic missiles carrying hundreds of kilograms of explosives, is shifting the focus from setting storage tanks on fire to physically destroying defense-industry workshops, propellant-production lines, microelectronics facilities, and irreplaceable CNC machine tools.

recentItems.title: 60 DELEGATIONS AND 16 LEADERS TAKE ON THE KREMLIN! Even China demands an end to Putinʼs war!
recentItems.description:
The record-breaking sixth summit of the Crimea Platform in New York brought together more than 60 delegations and 16 leaders. Participants declared all Russian so-called elections on the peninsula legally null and void and discussed Black Sea security with the participation of Egypt, India, and Türkiye.

Meanwhile, at the UN Security Council, Ukraine’s foreign minister warned of the risk of global hunger affecting 400 million people because 11 million tonnes of grain were being blocked.

During the meeting, Colombia condemned Russia’s invasion, the United States warned against escalation, China called for an immediate end to the fighting, and Ukraine and Türkiye urged an urgent reform of the UN Security Council and called for the aggressor to be stripped of its veto power.

recentItems.title: BRUTAL STRIKE ON KYIV: RUSSIANS KILL 14-YEAR-OLD BOY, DOZENS INJURED!
recentItems.description:
Russian forces struck a high-rise apartment building in Kyiv, killing a 14-year-old boy and injuring at least nine people. Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the attack an act of senseless terror and urged Ukraine’s partners to strengthen its air defenses.

Meanwhile, Finnish and Swedish fighter jets carried out their first joint interception of Russian aircraft near NATO borders, while Denmark’s intelligence service warned that Moscow was preparing a new wave of hybrid attacks and acts of sabotage against Europe.
